newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey, Ukraine sign oil pipeline agreement.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, Ukraine sign oil pipeline agreement.

text.p: Turkey and Ukraine signed a deal on Wednesday to build a pipeline from the Mediterranean to the Black Sea through Turkey to meet part of Ukraine's crude oil needs, by-passing the congested Turkish straits.

Turkey's state Anatolian news agency said the pipeline would be laid from Ceyhan, terminus of an oil pipeline from Iraq, to Samsun port on the Black Sea coast through the central Turkish towns of Kayseri, Sivas and Tokat.
The original studies suggested a 900-km (562-mile) pipeline would be built, passing through the refinery town of Kirikkale near Ankara.
The agreement was signed in Ankara by Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan and Ukraine's Anatoly Minchenko, state minister for industry policy and energy, the agency said.

Botas, Turkey's state pipeline company, and Ukraine's Ukrzakordonnaftogazbud company had been holding studies since July, 1994 for the pipeline, which will be 564 km (353 miles) long according to the modified route.
A joint venture to be set up by the companies will carry out the project, the agency said.
"The pipeline will by-pass the busy Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits and carry crude oil for Ukraine and other Black Sea countries from world markets," a Botas official said earlier.
Kutan was quoted by the agency as saying that the project envisaged building two terminals at Ceyhan and Samsun ports.
He said the cost of the pipeline would depend on its capacity. "We have not decided on whether the pipeline should be a single one or a twin pipeline," he said.

"If a pipeline that will carry 40 million tonnes of oil annually is built at the first stage, the cost will be $650 million. A second one to be built next to it with a 30-million-tonne capacity will mean another $450 million in investments," he said.
He said the eventual total capacity of the pipeline, which carry oil only in one direction -- to Ukraine -- would be 70 million tonnes a year.
"Turkey will get a transit fee of $5 per tonne carried. Turkey will earn between $75 million to $225 million annually from fees," Kutan said.
He said Ukraine would meet investment costs and Turkey would provide for other project costs, but did not elaborate.
Nearly 50,000 vessels a year transport oil and other goods through Turkey's two straits mainly for Russia, Balkan countries and other Black Sea ports.

About 60 million tonnes of crude oil and petroleum derivatives are annually carried through the straits, where several deadly sea accidents involving oil tankers in past years have led Turkey to seek other means for such transportation.
Kutan said the Ukraine pipeline project would not block efforts to persuade an international consortium that will develop Caspian and Kazakh oilfields to build a pipeline from Baku to Ceyhan.
